title: Minimum Operations to Make a Subsequence
summary: Given an array target consisting of distinct integers and an array arr that may contain duplicates, find the minimum number of insertions required into arr to make target a subsequence of arr.
statement: Given an array target consisting of distinct integers and an array arr that may contain duplicates, find the minimum number of insertions required into arr to make target a subsequence of arr. A subsequence is formed by removing some elements from the original array while maintaining the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: target contains distinct integers; arr may contain duplicates.
Insert the fewest values anywhere in arr so target becomes a subsequence.
hints: Distinct target values map the problem to keeping an increasing sequence of target indices.
Map arr values that occur in target, then find the LIS length.
Maintain minimal tail indices with lower-bound replacement; answer target length minus tails length.
Increasing mapped indices are exactly a target subsequence, and every missing target member needs one insertion.
editorial: Increasing mapped indices are exactly a target subsequence, and every missing target member needs one insertion.

tests.explanation: Only target value three is already in order, so two insertions are needed.
A longest target-ordered subsequence has length three, requiring three insertions.
